summary: Streaming session halts mid-response when adaptive fallback swaps worker under transient latency spike
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports SSE chat stream stops emitting tokens halfway through a response. Impact: Several active sessions (5 of 8) for Acme Analytics' dedicated pool experienced mid-generation halts during a 30-minute window causing partial responses and client-side timeouts. Environment: Dedicated pool (c-pool-7) in us-east serving rw-large-v2 fixed to model tag '2026-03-09-quant'.

Observed: When the platform triggered an adaptive fallback (worker swap to a quantized variant after a latency spike/batch eviction), some SSE sessions stopped producing tokens and the connection remained open with no further data for ~15-40s, then eventually closed by client. Expected: Fallback should continue streaming to the client without silent stalls; tokens should continue to stream from the new worker or an in-flight fallback route.

Timeline: 2026-03-12 15:08 UTC: Customer observed first stall; 15:09-15:40 UTC: pattern repeats across sessions; 15:45 UTC: Customer opened ticket.

Notes: This ticket focuses on streaming stalls correlated with adaptive fallback routing during transient per-worker latency spikes. The behaviour differs from proxy timeouts and from short SSE quiet periods: connection did not reset immediately and no 502/5xx was returned from gateway during the stall window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use dedicated pool c-pool-7 pinned to rw-large-v2 (tag 2026-03-09-quant)
2) Send multiple concurrent streaming chat requests with context lengths ~8k tokens and enable adaptive fallback in routing policy
3) Force a transient load spike on one worker (CPU/GPU saturate) or simulate eviction of a worker instance
4) Observe SSE/WSS stream: some streams halt mid-token when routing decides to swap worker to quantized fallback
5) Check request routing logs and worker handoff trace IDs
logs: Extracts: routing.trace=rt-88c2a; 2026-03-12T15:10:03Z: worker-43 latency 230ms -> routing decision: fallback to worker-87 (quant). 2026-03-12T15:10:03Z: stream-chunk: sent token chunk id=...; 2026-03-12T15:10:03Z: stream-state: handoff_initiated; 2026-03-12T15:10:03Z: socket: no write for 17s; 2026-03-12T15:10:20Z: routing.trace=rt-88c2a: handoff_complete; 2026-03-12T15:10:20Z: no further tokens observed by client. Gateway returned 200 until connection closed. Additional traces attached in support bundle (trace ids: rt-88c2a, rt-90b1f).
investigation_notes: Support triage: confirmed dedicated pool and model pinning; customer-side client keeps connection open and reports no network interruptions.
SRE findings: observed worker eviction events and rapid kernel-selection changes on fallback worker around stall time; async KV cache invalidation occurred during handoff.
Hypothesis 1: when fallback handoff occurs mid-stream the runtime's streaming buffer flush path isn't atomically resumed on new worker, causing a silent stall until timeout.
Hypothesis 2: proxy/gateway expects a small keepalive interval that was temporarily suppressed during handoff, resulting in connection considered alive but no chunks routed to client.

Repro attempt: internal test harness reproduced silent stall when inducing a worker swap within 50ms of a token flush boundary; observed identical pattern of 'handoff_initiated' then no token emission until handoff_complete but no downstream flush.
Related: see INT-4402 for previous internal notes about streaming flush race during live migration and SUP-332110 for similar stall patterns under burst load.
Interim mitigation: increased keepalive pulse frequency on proxy for affected pool and temporarily disabled adaptive fallback for c-pool-7 to prevent mid-response swaps.
Customer workaround: client reduced request parallelism and set a 60s client-side retry for partial responses; this reduced user-visible interruptions but did not eliminate the underlying fault.
resolution: In progress: engineering to implement atomic stream handoff that guarantees flush from source worker before releasing stream ownership. Planned patch to streaming runtime to serialize handoff and emit explicit 'handshake' tokens so clients can detect worker switch. Target deploy to staging 2026-03-17, canary to affected pool 2026-03-20.
